items.title: Inversion in If Clauses for Formal Writing
items.description: Learn how native speakers use inversion (Had I known, Were I to...) to sound more formal and sophisticated in academic and professional writing.

items.title: Fixing Dangling Modifiers
items.description: Identify and correct dangling modifiers—phrases that don't clearly connect to the word they modify—a common IELTS Writing Task 1 error.

items.title: Reported Questions Without 'Do'
items.description: Master the grammar of reported questions (He asked if she had finished) and how to avoid the common mistake of adding 'do'.

items.title: Cleft Sentences for Emphasis and Variation
items.description: Use cleft sentences (It was the policy that caused the problem) to add emphasis and structural variety to your essays.

items.title: Ellipsis and Substitution for Coherence
items.description: Learn how professional writers use ellipsis (leaving out words) and substitution (using 'one', 'do') to create smooth, cohesive paragraph flow.

items.title: Reducing Adverbial Clauses: Principles and Practice
items.description: Transform long adverbial clauses into shorter reduced forms (Being aware that... → Aware that...) to improve sentence efficiency.

items.title: Subjunctive Mood After Suggest, Recommend, Insist
items.description: Understand when and how to use subjunctive forms (I suggest that she attend, not attends) in academic and formal writing.

items.title: Fronting Adverbials for Rhetorical Effect
items.description: Move adverbials to sentence-initial position (Clearly, the evidence shows...) to create emphasis and control reader focus in persuasive writing.

items.title: Noun Markers and Determiners for Precise Reference
items.description: Use determiners (articles, demonstratives, quantifiers) correctly to make specific, clear claims in academic arguments.

items.title: Transitivity and Voice Choice in Academic Discourse
items.description: Understand how choosing transitive vs. intransitive verbs, and active vs. passive voice, affects meaning and tone in professional writing.

items.title: Tense Sequencing in Narrative and Chronological Explanation
items.description: Manage multiple tenses correctly when describing historical events or sequential procedures (He was working when she arrived earlier that day).

items.title: Discourse Deixis: 'This', 'That', 'There' and Paragraph Cohesion
items.description: Use demonstrative and spatial deixis (This finding suggests..., There remains one issue...) to create clear links between sentences and paragraphs.

items.title: Subject-Verb Concord: Complex and Tricky Cases
items.description: Master agreement with collective nouns, plural forms with singular meaning, and phrases like 'neither...nor' and 'one of the...'
